title: Magnetic fusion confinement with tokamaks and stellarators
summary: IAEA explains magnetic confinement and distinguishes tokamaks and stellarators as the most common magnetic-confinement devices. Used to support route separation, not plant readiness.
limitations: Broad expert overview; it does not validate a commercial plant, cost, availability, or a specific investable supplier exposure.

title: Approaches to Fusion
summary: Overview source distinguishing magnetic, inertial, Z-pinch, accelerator/plasma-collision, and piston/compression approaches. Used to justify a route portfolio rather than a single fusion route.
limitations: High-level overview; not a reviewed engineering decomposition or investment source.

title: ITER - the way to new energy
summary: ITER describes the goal of demonstrating fusion power production at power-plant scale and reactor technology. Used to support tokamak route context and ITER as an international project, not a commercial product.
limitations: ITER is an experimental international project and does not generate electricity as a commercial plant; do not treat it as commercial viability proof.

title: ITER Blanket
summary: ITER's blanket page describes blanket modules, first-wall heat load removal, actively cooled blanket operation, neutron shielding, heat extraction, and later tritium-breeding module tests. Used to support shared blanket/PFC/divertor constraints, not commercial plant readiness.
limitations: Reviewed only for the existence and technical role of ITER blanket/first-wall heat-removal and TBM testing. It does not validate commercial availability, cost, tritium self-sufficiency, or any supplier exposure.

title: ITER Disruption Mitigation
summary: ITER describes disruptions as tokamak plasma instabilities that can cause thermal loading, melting, mechanical strain, and component lifetime risk, and describes disruption mitigation as a supporting system requirement.
limitations: Official ITER technology page; does not validate commercial tokamak availability, cost, or public supplier exposure.

title: Wendelstein 7-X
sourceName: Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics
summary: IPP describes Wendelstein 7-X as the world's largest stellarator, with a core system of non-planar superconducting magnet coils used to test power-plant suitability.
limitations: Research device evidence; does not prove a commercial stellarator plant, cost, maintainability, or supplier exposure.

title: What Is NIF?
summary: LLNL describes NIF as a laser-based inertial confinement facility. Used to support laser ICF as a distinct route with laser-driver and target-compression dependencies.
limitations: NIF ignition and target gain are not plant net-electric gain; this source does not validate commercial IFE economics.

title: Livermore Inertial Fusion Energy references
summary: LLNL reference index for inertial fusion energy topics including target design, chamber, fuel cycle, and plant-relevant research directions.
limitations: Reference index; individual technical claims require exact paper-level review.

title: Target Fabrication
summary: LLNL/LIFT describes inertial fusion energy power-plant targets as needing standard, low-cost designs that can be mass-produced at very high quantities, while current targets are precision proof-of-principle devices requiring further R&D.
limitations: Research-program page; not a commercial target-factory proof or supplier exposure source.

title: Fusion Power Technology
summary: General Fusion describes its magnetized target fusion approach combining plasma physics, mechanical compression, and liquid metal systems.
limitations: Company source; performance, cost, timing, and plant-level viability are vendor claims until independently reviewed.

title: The Field Reversed Configuration
summary: TAE describes the field-reversed configuration as its fusion-machine route. Used to support FRC as a distinct route and TAE as a private route builder.
limitations: Company source; route performance and commercialization timing are vendor claims.

title: Helion technology
summary: Helion describes its fusion technology around compact pulsed plasma systems. Used only as vendor evidence for a private FRC-style route builder.
limitations: Company source; do not treat as independent validation of commercial readiness or public-market exposure.

title: Sandia Z Machine
summary: Sandia's Z Machine source supports pulsed-power and Z-machine context for Z-pinch or magnetically driven inertial fusion research.
limitations: National-lab facility source; not a commercial Z-pinch power-plant validation.

title: How It Works
summary: Zap Energy describes sheared-flow stabilization for a Z-pinch fusion route. Used as vendor evidence for route-specific MHD stability and Zap as a private route builder.
limitations: Company source; route maturity, economics, and durability remain unreviewed vendor claims.

title: Retrospective of the ARPA-E ALPHA Fusion Program
summary: OSTI record for ARPA-E ALPHA program retrospective, useful for lower-cost alternative fusion approach framing and unreviewed secondary-route context.
limitations: Program retrospective source; not claim-level support for any specific current company timeline or supplier exposure.

title: Tritium Breeding
summary: ITER describes lithium-bearing breeding blankets, test blanket modules, tritium extraction, closed fuel-cycle experiments, and the need for future fusion plants to breed their own tritium. Used to support tritium breeding as a shared D-T plant constraint.
limitations: Reviewed only for the need to breed tritium and for ITER TBM/fuel-cycle testing context. It does not demonstrate commercial-scale tritium production, recycling, or plant readiness.

title: Technical Meeting on Tritium Breeding Blankets and Associated Neutronics
summary: IAEA frames tritium breeding blankets and associated neutronics as important novel components for next-step devices after ITER, including design, fabrication, integration, operation, reliability, availability, and qualification issues.
limitations: Reviewed only for expert framing that breeding blankets/neutronics remain important design, fabrication, integration, operation, reliability, availability, and qualification issues. Not a reviewed plant design or commercial supplier validation.

title: High-Energy X-Rays Open a New View of Degradation in Potential Fusion Reactor Material
summary: DOE describes degradation of fusion reactor core structural materials under energetic neutron bombardment as a major hurdle and notes that qualification relies on simulated environments because no fusion devices exist for experimental materials research.
limitations: Reviewed only for fusion-neutron material degradation and qualification-gap framing. Not route-specific commercial readiness, cost, or supplier exposure proof.

title: The state of the art for DEMO
summary: EUROfusion summarizes DEMO design work and identifies remote maintenance, tritium breeding, breeding-blanket heat extraction, plasma-facing materials, magnet design, nuclear safety, and integration as essential demonstration-plant topics.
limitations: DEMO design-status source; it does not validate commercial cost, timeline, or public equity exposure.
